questions.prompt: The Magna Carta was signed at which location?
questions.fact: The site was chosen as neutral ground in a meadow, because neither the barons nor the king trusted the other indoors.

questions.prompt: How many pairs of chromosomes does a typical human cell contain?
questions.fact: Chimpanzees have 24 pairs. Two of theirs fused into one of ours, and the seam is still visible in the sequence.

questions.prompt: Which sport features terms like pin, escape and takedown?
questions.fact: It appeared in the ancient Olympics and is one of very few sports on the programme of the first modern Games too.

questions.prompt: Which television talent show format originated in the United Kingdom in 2001?
questions.fact: It became American Idol a year later, and the format has since been licensed to over forty countries.

questions.prompt: Which capital city sits on the Tiber river?
questions.fact: The river's flooding was so destructive that high walls were built along it in the 1870s, cutting the city off from its own water.

questions.prompt: Which term describes the turning point of a narrative?
questions.fact: In classical structure it sits at the centre, not the end, with everything after it working out the consequences.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym QR stand for in QR code?
questions.fact: It was invented to track car parts, and its creator chose not to enforce the patent, which is why it spread everywhere.
